column1: # Key families of the domain (P/06.7 N1.11 families): families(decls, present) → {<id>: [<key>…]}.
# decls — domain.keys of the catalogue's manifests as JSON text {<sub>: [{id, keys?, prefix?}]}; present — the keys of the rows under domain/
# of this store, a JSON array (the order does not matter). expect — families: the union of the keys of an id over all manifests, without repeats,
# ascending by the bytes of UTF-8 (C06-DOMAIN-KEY-FAMILIES-168-21). A row: case<TAB>decls<TAB>present<TAB>expect<TAB>note.

column5: one manifest, no declared keys: the id with an empty list (sc. 06 step 2)
the named key and the keys under prefix; other rows of domain/ do not enter
one id in two manifests: the union; testsub/ before testsub2/ (0x2f < 0x32)
the same input in another order of manifests and rows: the same answer
the second manifest has no keys here: the keys of the first stay
the first manifest has no keys here: the keys of the second are not dropped
neither manifest has keys here: an empty list
the common id is united, the own ids of each manifest — as is
the named key lies under prefix as well: once
under prefix — only the keys beginning with its bytes; t and tx without the named key do not enter
ascending by bytes: B (0x42) < a-1 (0x2d) < a.1 (0x2e) < a_1 (0x5f) < b
bytes of UTF-8, not UTF-16 code units: é (C3) < ｚ (EF) < 😀 (F0); in UTF-16 😀 (D83D) would come before ｚ

column1: # --- judge-only: case descriptions and expected outcomes moved here (ADR-0133 add. (4)) from the chapter README and norms N5; not a rule source ---
# 12 rows: one manifest (no keys — an empty list, sc. 06 step 2; a named key and keys under `prefix`); one `id` in two

# `id` next to their own ones; a named key under `prefix` — once; `prefix` — by bytes; the order is ascending by UTF-8 bytes
# (ASCII and non-BMP: 😀 after ｚ, although in UTF-16 it would come earlier).
